speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower how many workers have successfully found jobs through Government-supported job fairs each year over the past 10 years.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: In assisting our jobseekers, we make a special effort to help older jobseekers and the long-term unemployed, as I have mentioned earlier, and the outcome has been encouraging.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Over the years, the profile of workers placed by our career centres has become more inclusive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: As I have mentioned, we pay special attention to them and, as a result, of all the successful jobseekers we served last year, 35% were previously long-term unemployed.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: Through continued efforts with our tripartite partners, we will strive to quicken the transformation of industry to create better jobs and, at the same time, quicken the re-development of our workforce to create better skills.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
text: We will also keep strengthening our career matching services to minimise missed matches and mismatches in the local market as we go through this period of economic transition.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For these job fairs, is there a mechanism to ensure that employers who participate have a minimum number of jobs that are up for offer before they are actually allowed to participate in these fairs?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Over the last 10 years, the numbers fluctuated up and down.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It all depends on how many jobseekers came to us.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Jobseekers who need help, they just have to come to us and we will respond accordingly.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Jobseekers coming to us to look for jobs, we will help them in various ways.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For every jobseeker, we look at his or her skills profile, career interest, and we look for a suitable job for him.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In some cases, it is group to group.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, a company has a retrenchment exercise, 20 workers were retrenched.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the group of 20 workers, we look for a group of employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will bring the employers to the company to do a group-to-group matching and try to help the 20 workers to find 20 jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other cases, we go for the "many to many" approach.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In some cases, jobseekers are not looking to work but we want to encourage them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, in a community, we want to encourage more of our older residents to take on employment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, we would bring employers with jobs in the community to the Community Centre to draw them out.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, we have residents with no intention to work, but having attended our job fair, they said, "Oh, I did not know that nearby there are such job openings." So, this is the first objective.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The second objective is that we have jobseekers who are not active jobseekers or what we call the passive jobseekers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They have jobs today, they are not in a hurry to get a job.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: But they would like to know what is available.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For example, when we organise a job fair with the hotel industry, many workers from other sectors come to attend and understand better where the hotel sector is heading  in case one day they need to move on to this sector.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of course, lastly, those who are looking for jobs.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the part of the employers, we leave it to them to compete for the workers.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
